picks.file: Vue de Caen capitale de la Basse Normandie . Vue exécutée par les soins de Philippe Buache, sur les desseins de Mr. de La Londe - btv1b531816318 (1 of 2).jpg
picks.what: View of the city from the south, engraving (Bibliothèque nationale de France)
picks.who: Philippe Buache after drawings by de La Londe
picks.why: full skyline with the abbey and church spires; dated January 1747

picks.file: William Fowler - Vue de l eglise Saint-Pierre et de l Odon - Caen MBA inv. 395.jpg
picks.what: The church of Saint-Pierre and the Odon, painting (Musée des Beaux-Arts de Caen)
picks.why: color; Saint-Pierre’s spire over the river, now covered over

picks.what: General view from the Abbaye aux Dames, photochrom print (Library of Congress)
picks.why: color view over the roofs, Saint-Gilles in front, Saint-Pierre and Saint-Étienne spires beyond

picks.file: The British Army in Normandy 1944 B6714.jpg
picks.what: The bombed city center, photograph (Imperial War Museum)
picks.who: No 5 Army Film and Photographic Unit
picks.why: only P5 view with a firm date; the ruined center on 9 July 1944

picks.what: The castle and the church of Saint-Pierre, photograph
picks.why: two landmarks that say Caen in one frame

gaps: P0–P1: none; P2 only 1747 (the 1657 Merian item is a flat street plan)
notes: #2 is the same 1747 plate with a wider paper margin; #4 is its blank back. #11 and #12 are the same photochrom; #11 is the Library of Congress copy. #15 (station postcard) skipped: dated only ‘before 1914’. #16 is low resolution (1215 px) and marked as an event; the Isabey lithograph of 1832 (#5–#7, the same print in three museums) is a fallback for P3 if the Fowler painting is not wanted.
